title: stability-integrator-playbook-and-critical-path-2026-05
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a cross-functional execution plan for the Stability Integrator initiative — a focused program to operationalize SLOs across critical Redwood services and validate the reliability guardrails via a small pilot. The doc is intended for eng leads, platform, product-hosted-api, solutions engineering, SRE oncall, and program managers.

Background & problem statement:
- Multiple services have informal availability targets but lack a consistent SLO design, ownership, and operational runbook.
- On-call teams lack clear escalation boundaries when SLOs degrade; no standard rollback or canary policy tied to SLO regressions.
- Platform teams need an integration pattern to expose metrics and alerts in a way feature teams can adopt without large infra lifts.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: design + pilot for 3 critical services (api-gateway, embedding-store, realtime-router); SLO definition, alerting, dashboards, runbooks, incident playbook integration, and a single canary rollback flow tied to SLO breach thresholds.
- Out-of-scope: global infra migrations, billing changes, or new agent-level SLAs.

Top-level goals (OKR-aligned):
1) Consistently measure and enforce availability and latency SLOs for pilot services by end of Q3 2026.
2) Validate a rollback/canary policy that reduces customer-facing degradations by 40% in pilot window.
3) Deliver an "SLO integrator" template (metrics + dashboard + runbook) that can be adopted by 80% of teams within 6 weeks of release.

Success metrics / signals of readiness:
- Each pilot service emits SLO-aligned metrics and a dedicated dashboard (latency percentiles, error budget burn rate) by pilot launch date.
- Average time-to-detect for SLO degradations <= 120s.
- First-time adoption of integrator template by a non-pilot team within 30 days.
- Post-pilot retro indicates < 2 unresolvable dependencies blocking full rollout.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Stability Integrator (program lead): Aisha Patel — coordinates cross-functional work, maintains plan, runs weekly unblockers.
- Pilot Service Owners: (api-gateway: Diego Morales, embedding-store: Rina Saito, realtime-router: Marcus Li) — define SLOs, approve runbooks, validate metrics.
- Platform telemetry: Tara O'Connell — ensure metrics ingestion, template dashboards, and SLI instrumentation guidance.
- Product-hosted-api: Priya Shah — customer-impact assessment, acceptance criteria for rollouts.
- Solutions Eng & CS: rotation for customer-facing signoff and rollback playbook testing.
- SRE oncall: provides runbook feedback and participates in simulated breaches during the pilot.

Timeline & critical path (highest-priority dependencies highlighted):
Phase 0 — Prep (Weeks 0-2):
- Kickoff + alignment workshop (owner: Aisha) — confirm pilot services and owners.
- Telemetry gap analysis (owner: Tara) — list missing SLIs (critical path).
- Security & access review for dashboards (owner: Marcus).

Phase 1 — Instrumentation & Baseline (Weeks 3-6):
- Implement missing SLIs (owner: service owners, dependency: platform telemetry).
- Baseline data collection (14 days of steady-state traffic).
- Draft SLOs & error budget policies (owner: service owners + product-hosted-api).

Phase 2 — SLOs + Alerts + Runbooks (Weeks 7-10):
- Finalize SLOs and alert thresholds (target: p99 latency, p50, and error-rate SLOs where relevant).
- Create runbooks that map alert -> triage -> mitigation -> rollback steps.
- Integrator dashboard template release (owner: Tara).

Phase 3 — Canary/Automation & Simulation (Weeks 11-14):
- Implement automated canary promotion/rollback tooling (dependency: release-engineering).
- Run two scheduled breach simulations (SRE oncall + service owners) and collect metrics.
- Update runbooks based on simulation lessons.

Phase 4 — Pilot launch & monitoring (Weeks 15-20):
- Soft launch: route 5-10% traffic through canary path, watch error budget burn, collect customer-impact signals.
- Decision gate at Week 18 for full rollout or pause (criteria: error budget burn < 10% per week and no critical customer incidents).
- Full rollout if criteria met; otherwise, pause and remediate.

Milestones & dates (example calendar):
- 2026-05-12: Kickoff (done)
- 2026-05-18: Telemetry gap doc (RDW-2183) published
- 2026-06-02: Baseline collection complete
- 2026-06-23: Runbooks + dashboard template v1 ready
- 2026-07-14: Canary tooling integrated into release flow
- 2026-08-01: Pilot soft launch
- 2026-08-18: Pilot decision gate

Risk catalog (top 6 risks & mitigations):
1) Missing SLIs or noisy instrumentation -> mitigation: telemetry freeze window + prioritized infra tickets; fallback: synthetic tests for missing signals.
2) Release engineering integration delays -> mitigation: early spike and fixed engineering owner; plan B: manual promotion workflow.
3) Alert fatigue from spurious SLO alerts -> mitigation: temporary alert dampening for pilot and tighten thresholds after baseline.
4) Cross-team communication breakdown during incident -> mitigation: pre-assigned liaison for each team + clear escalation matrix in runbook.
5) Customer-impact not captured by internal metrics -> mitigation: add product-level indicators and CS warm path for customer reports.
6) Post-failure cascading rollbacks -> mitigation: staged rollback + circuit-breaker thresholds and explicit manual confirm step.

SLO design patterns (recommended templates):
- Availability SLO: "successful_request_rate" measured at service boundary over a 7-day rolling window, target 99.9% for api-gateway pilot.
- Latency SLO: p99 latency target with tiers (fast-path p50 target for the realtime-router).
- Error budget policy: burn actions at 5%/day, 10%/week thresholds. If weekly burn > 10% -> pause non-critical deploys.

Alerting & oncall flow (summary):
- Signal -> burn-rate alert -> SRE triage -> service owner notification -> if burn persists 30m -> product-hosted-api escalation and canary rollback trigger.
- All escalations documented as templates in the runbook; Slack channel #sre-stability-integrator enabled for alerts + postmortem threads.

Runbook & handoff checklist (must-haves before pilot launch):
- SLO definition doc linked in service repo.
- Dashboards with named owners and read permissions.
- Automated or documented manual rollback flow tested in staging.
- Contact list for liaisons and escalation chain.
- Postmortem template and retro cadence scheduled.

Pilot acceptance criteria (go/no-go):
- Observability: required SLIs emitted and dashboards show >14 days baseline.
- Reliability: simulated breaches show expected runbook actions complete within 45 minutes.
- Safety: rollback flow validated and can be executed without data loss.
- Customer impact: no >SEV2 customer incidents during 2-week soft launch.

Communication plan:
- Weekly sync (30m) led by Aisha — standing invite to service owners, platform telemetry, release-engineering, product-hosted-api, CS rotation.
- Status notes to #sre-stability-integrator every Friday summarizing errors, burn rate, and blockers.
- Bi-weekly executive snapshot for eng leadership with 3-line summary and top risks.

Post-pilot: adoption roadmap & handoff:
- Package integrator template as a short "onboarding kit": step-by-step checklist, sample runbooks, Terraform snippets for dashboards, and a 2-week office hours schedule for teams adopting.
- Handoff to Reliability Enablement (SRE enablement) with a playbook and a migration timeline for remaining services (target 12 months).

Open questions & decisions to track (working backlog):
- Which exact percentiles and windows should be standard across all services for latency SLOs? (proposal: p90/p99 with 7d window)
- Are non-customer-facing internal APIs eligible for relaxed SLOs? (decision needed by product-hosted-api)
- Confirm retention of high-resolution metrics for 90 days vs 30 days (cost tradeoff).

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Tara to publish telemetry gap list (RDW-2183) by 2026-05-18.
- Service owners to draft SLO proposals for review in next sync.
- Release-eng to schedule a 2-hour spike for canary automation feasibility (owner: Marcus).

Appendix: useful links & artifacts:
- Confluence: STABILITY-INTEGRATOR-LANDING (see linked_artifacts)
- JIRA epic: RDW-2183 (Pilot telemetry + SLOs)
- GitHub PR: infra/pull/562 (canary tooling spike)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an intentionally compact operational plan aimed at a 3-month pilot. Feedback requested on: pilot scope, rollback criteria, and acceptance thresholds.
- If you have concerns about the pilot dates above, propose alternatives in comments or in the next sync.
